state_profile.voting_summary: Indiana votes about evenly across election day and 28 days of in-person absentee (early) voting, with mail requiring an excuse (5%). Polls close at 6 p.m. Eastern in most of the state (7 p.m. in the Central-time corners) (the first closures in the nation) and early/absentee votes are released first, with election day precincts following quickly; results are largely complete by late evening. Early voting ran R+24 and election day R+35, so the earliest numbers understate the final Republican margin slightly.
